samples.summary: No test that `verifyYorkieToken` accepts the new `yorkie-service` token, and nothing exercises mint→verify end to end
samples.evidence: `AuthService.verifyYorkieToken` gained a third accepted `typ` (auth.service.ts:99-105), and the whole feature depends on a token minted by `signYorkieServiceToken` (yorkie-service-token.ts:38, signed with the caller-supplied `JWT_SECRET`) verifying through `AuthService` (which uses `accessSecret` = `JWT_SECRET`). The `Yorkie tokens` describe block in auth.service.spec.ts (lines 59-105) round-trips only `issueYorkieUserToken` and `issueYorkieShareToken`; I found no case constructing a service token. The controller spec cannot cover it — `makeController` stubs `verifyYorkieToken` wholesale (yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:22-29) and simply returns `{typ:'yorkie-service'}`. yorkie.service.spec.ts:186-190 verifies the minted token with a bare `new JwtService().verify(...)`, not through `AuthService`, so the two halves are never proved to agree. If they diverge (secret source, `typ` constant, claim shape) every server-side attach 401s on any deployment with the webhook registered — v1 content endpoints, `DocumentCopyService`, template publish/seed — and the suite stays green.

samples.summary: `still refuses a service token that does not verify` is a duplicate of an existing test and exercises nothing service-token-specific
samples.evidence: The case builds `makeController({ identity: 'throw' })` and sends token `'forged'`. The stub throws for any token regardless of its content (lines 22-29), so this is byte-for-byte the same code path as `401s on an invalid/expired token for a doc method` (line 99) with a different string literal. It would pass identically if the `yorkie-service` branch in `decide` were removed, made unconditional, or if forged-token handling regressed — the token string is never parsed. It is presented (via its title and the surrounding comment) as coverage that a forged service token is refused, which it does not provide.

samples.summary: The read-only editor test's `canUndo`/`undo`-spy assertions hold regardless of the new `readOnly` guards
samples.evidence: `lets no write reach the store on a read-only mount` starts from `new MemNoteStore('hello')` with an empty undo stack, so `store.canUndo()` is already `false`; `expect(api.canUndo()).toBe(false)` (and `canRedo`) passes whether or not the new `!readOnly &&` in editor.ts:672-674 exists. Likewise `expect(undo).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`: `initialize` wraps the store in `readOnlyNoteStore`, whose `undo` is replaced by `noHistory`, so the spy is unreachable even if `if (readOnly) return;` in `runHistory` (editor.ts:345) were deleted. To be non-vacuous the test would need pre-existing history (e.g. `store.editText(...)` before `initialize`) and then assert `api.canUndo() === false` while `store.canUndo() === true`. Impact if the guard regressed: a viewer mount offers an enabled undo/redo control that does nothing.

samples.summary: `neuters every write path` does not actually observe `setLocalSelection` (or `recordSelectionForHistory`) being neutered, and reader forwarding of a truthy `canUndo` is untested
samples.evidence: `view.setLocalSelection(1, 2)` is called but nothing asserts its effect; in `MemNoteStore` it only sets the private `currentSelection`, which no assertion in the test reads, so the case passes whether or not `setLocalSelection` is forwarded to the target. The module comment (read-only.ts:170-174) calls this neutering deliberate (a viewer's caret must not be published via `doc.update`), so it is the one write with a user-visible privacy consequence and it has no assertion. Similarly `subscribePresence` is in the readers allowlist but never called in any test, and `canUndo`/`canRedo` are only asserted as `false` (line 20 and line 46) — a regression that dropped them from `NOTE_STORE_READERS` (returning the `noop`'s `undefined`, or `false`) would not fail anything.
searchedFor: read packages/notes/src/store/memory.ts to check observability of setLocalSelection

samples.summary: The divider changes (25px hit area, `touch-action: none`, new `track` ratio math) have no test
samples.evidence: `onDividerPointerDown` now computes `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth` and derives `splitRatio` from it, and the divider gained `boxSizing`, a 25px width with 12px padding, and `touchAction = 'none'`. Grepping `divider|splitRatio|touchAction|note-divider` across packages/notes/src returns only editor.ts — no test file mentions them, and packages/notes has no drag/interaction test (unlike slides' `interactions/*.test.ts`). The pane ratio is directly user-visible (the divider trailing the pointer was the stated bug), and the geometry is testable in jsdom by stubbing `getBoundingClientRect` and defining `offsetWidth`. Failure is contained to a mis-tracking split pane.

samples.summary: `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` and the `JWT_SECRET`-missing branch of `YorkieService` are untested
samples.evidence: `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` is the injector for all three ops scripts (copy-yorkie-documents.ts:232/238, migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:221, migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:347); no spec file exists for `yorkie-service-token.ts` (Glob of packages/backend/src/yorkie/*.ts shows no `yorkie-service-token.spec.ts`) and grep finds no test importing it. Neither the `process.env.JWT_SECRET` fallback, the `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` fallback, nor the `undefined`-with-warning path is exercised. The same is true of the new else-branch in `YorkieService`'s constructor (yorkie.service.ts) — yorkie.service.spec.ts's mock config always returns a secret, so the warn/no-injector branch has no coverage. Also new CLI flags `--source-jwt-secret` / `--target-jwt-secret` in `parseArgs` have no test (no test file references copy-yorkie-documents).

samples.summary: The frontend mount's own `readOnlyNoteStore` wrapping has no test
samples.evidence: `notes-view.tsx` now wraps `YorkieNoteStore` in `readOnlyNoteStore` when `readOnly`, and `storeRef` was widened to `NoteStore`. Glob of packages/frontend/src/app/notes/*.test.tsx returns only `notes-toolbar.test.tsx`; no test renders `NotesView`, and the new `shared-notes-layout.test.tsx` mocks `@/app/notes/notes-view` away entirely, so nothing asserts a viewer mount receives a guarded handle. The guarantee is duplicated by `initialize()` inside the engine (which is tested), so a regression here is contained — but the mount's own claim is unverified.

samples.summary: `hands the share-token uploader to the view` asserts a mock's return value
samples.evidence: `@/app/docs/image-insert` is mocked to `shareTokenImageUploader: (token) => async () => `uploaded:${token}`` and the test then asserts the resolved value is `"uploaded:tok-1"`. That only proves the token string was threaded into the (mocked) factory; nothing about the real uploader is exercised. Acceptable given the layout is what's under test, but the assertion's apparent strength comes from the mock, not the code.

samples.summary: `expect(said).not.toContain('token=')` can never have failed for this log line
samples.evidence: The shadow log template (`yorkie-auth.controller.ts:180`) has never contained a `token=` segment, and the test's token is the string `'t'`, so the negative assertion holds trivially. Harmless as a regression guard, but it reads as verified redaction of a bearer credential when nothing redacts anything.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. auth.service.ts:95-107 adds YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE as a third accepted typ in verifyYorkieToken (secret = accessSecret/JWT_SECRET, line 58), but auth.service.spec.ts:59-105 only round-trips issueYorkieUserToken and issueYorkieShareToken plus negative cases; no test feeds a service token to verifyYorkieToken. A repo-wide grep for 'yorkie-service'/'YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE' shows no spec file imports yorkie-service-token.ts anywhere. The mint-side test (yorkie.service.spec.ts:176-191) validates the token with a bare `new JwtService().verify(...)`, not through AuthService, and yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts stubs verifyYorkieToken in all three construction sites (lines 23-29, 292, 324), so its 'allows the backend service token' case (119-128) starts from a fabricated identity. I also checked indirect paths: the only e2e suite that registers the webhook (test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:337-460) mints user tokens via issueYorkieUserToken (422, 499); the suites that attach via a real YorkieService (document-copy-attached.e2e-spec.ts:44-51, docs-tree-attached, docs-font-styles-attached) run against a Yorkie with no webhook methods registered, and all other e2e suites overrideProvider(YorkieService). Blocking under this lens: a changed authorization guard with zero meaningful coverage — inverting or dropping the new typ clause would keep the suite green while every server-side attach 401s where the webhook is registered.

finding.summary: No test joins the new service-token signer to the verifier that must accept it
finding.evidence: `auth.service.ts` was changed so `verifyYorkieToken` accepts `typ === YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE`, and `yorkie-service-token.ts` mints that token with its own DI-free `JwtService`. The `describe('Yorkie tokens')` block in auth.service.spec.ts (lines 59–105) round-trips only `issueYorkieUserToken` and `issueYorkieShareToken`; there is no case feeding `signYorkieServiceToken(secret, ...)` into `service.verifyYorkieToken(...)`. The only place a service token is verified in tests is yorkie.service.spec.ts:189, which uses a bare `new JwtService().verify(...)` rather than `AuthService`, so the two ends are never connected. The controller spec that exercises the new allow-branch (yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:123) stubs `verifyYorkieToken` out entirely. If the signing and verifying halves ever disagree (secret source, claim shape, expiry option, an added issuer/audience check), every server-side attach — v1 content endpoints, DocumentCopyService, template publish/seed — 401s on any deployment that registered the webhook methods, and nothing in the suite would notice.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `signYorkieServiceToken` (yorkie-service-token.ts:38-46) mints the token with its own module-local JwtService, and `AuthService.verifyYorkieToken` (auth.service.ts:95-107) was extended to accept `typ === YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE`. No test connects the two ends. The `Yorkie tokens` describe block (auth.service.spec.ts:59-105) round-trips only user and share tokens. Repo-wide grep for signYorkieServiceToken / yorkieServiceTokenInjector / YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE / 'yorkie-service' shows the only test touches are (a) yorkie.service.spec.ts:176-191, which decodes the injector's token with a bare `new JwtService().verify(...)` rather than AuthService, and (b) yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:119-132, where the controller's `verifyYorkieToken` is a jest stub (spec lines 23-29) so the real type check never executes. No spec file imports yorkie-service-token; real AuthService instances appear only in auth.service.spec.ts and revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:360, and that e2e is `it.skip` (line 258) and uses user tokens. The only enforcement-enabled e2e is that same skipped test. So the accept-branch for the service token type and the signed token's claim shape/secret/expiry are covered by nothing end-to-end; a mismatch between signer and verifier would ship green while 401-ing every server-side attach on a webhook-registered deployment. This is a genuine missing-test gap over changed, user-affecting behavior, squarely in the test-adequacy lane.
